newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner gets okay to offer local phone service.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner gets okay to offer local phone service.

text.p: The Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission said Wednesday it would allow a subsidiary of Time Warner Inc to compete for local telecommunications customers in the state.

The commission allowed Time Warner Communications of Indiana Inc to offer local service using its own facilities and on a resale basis. Time Warner will compete with Ameritech Corp, GTE Corp and Sprint Corp.
Time Warner has already installed some telecommunications facilities and plans to expand them, the commission said.

Time Warner will purchase services at a 21 percent discount from Ameritech's retail rates and at a 17 percent discount from GTE's retail rates. The commission said a rate has not been established for Sprint. The rates are interim and subject to modification.
Ameritech is the state's largest exchange company with more than 2.2 million access lines. GTE has more than 800,000 lines and Sprint has more than 219,000, the commission said.

Time Warner has provided some telecommunications services in Indiana since 1987 under the name Indiana Digital Access. Time Warner became affiliated with US West Communications Group in 1994 and currently serves 91 Indiana customers.
